requirement:
An outline input MUST be rewritten only if the mapped node exists and its
structural hash, computed under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash` over the
{term}`requirements.refactor.mapped_back` text of the node, equals the recorded
hash.
rationale:
**Obligation.** An outline input is rewritten only if (a) the mapped node exists and (b) its structural hash, computed over the mapped-back text of the node, equals the recorded hash.

**Implementation.** `src/refactor.rs#fn[rewrite_input]` carries the `{impl}` reference. Its `InputSelector::Outline` branch does the following:
- It takes the recorded hash from the input. It maps `(file, item)` to the new address with `mappings.node`.
- It computes `back = states.hash(&states.outlines_back, new_file, new_item)`. `States::hash` parses the file and calls `parsed.resolve(file, item)`, which returns an error if the node is missing. This covers condition (a).
- `States::compute` builds `outlines_back` from file contents run through `mappings.text_back`, which is the mapped-back text. The back-overrides are inserted only when the reverted text differs from the file on disk. Otherwise the on-disk file is already the mapped-back text.
- It rewrites the input to the new address and the current hash (`outlines_post`) only when `back == recorded`. This covers condition (b).
- If the node is missing, it returns an error. If the hash differs, it returns "no longer has the recorded hash". In both cases the record is not rewritten.
- If no mapping affects the input, it returns `None` and leaves the input alone.

The `Mappings::text_back` helper, reached from `States::compute`, implements the mapped-back form. The structural hash itself is a cited requirement, so I did not reassess it.

**Tests.**
- `src/refactor/tests.rs#fn[mapped_back_text_replaces_whole_new_names_and_paths]` tests the mapped-back text transformation.
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_moved_function_keeps_its_evidence_current]` covers a moved node whose hash matches. It checks that the input is rewritten and that unaffected records are untouched.
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_function_edited_while_moving_leaves_its_records_stale]` covers a hash mismatch. It checks that the record is not rewritten and a stale report is produced.
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[an_input_whose_node_is_missing_after_the_move_is_not_rewritten]` covers a missing mapped node. It checks that the record is unchanged and an error is reported.
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_rename_rewrites_the_hash_of_a_node_whose_doc_comment_names_it]` covers a hash that depends on mapped-back text. A doc comment contains a renamed requirement name, and the test checks that the recorded hash is matched against the mapped-back text and the new hash is written.

All four obligations and the failure cases have tests that carry `{test}` references to the subject. I found no gaps.

text: :::{req} outline_inputs
An outline input MUST be rewritten only if the mapped node exists and its
structural hash, computed under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash` over the
{term}`requirements.refactor.mapped_back` text of the node, equals the recorded
hash.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{definition} mapped_back
:phrase: mapped-back
The *mapped-back* form of current text or a current address is the text or
address with each new side of the mappings replaced by its old side.
